challenge.better_approach: Considered: have cast_ticket itself run the check (that puts an inference call in the base cast door for every caster and reaches into codemother from base), or have the BUILDME lane run it on demand (a gate that writes). Calling the published CLI from the one automatic caster is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That one Haiku read per red is affordable in a batch. Measured: in commons origin/main the tester has made 2 cast commits, each casting 1 ticket. A whole-tree orphan scan could cast more; the reads are sequential, at most 2 per ticket.
challenge.prior_art: c66b25d122e6 built the check and the /sorted instruction to run it after each cast. 207c4074b3d5 built red_tickets and its commit-in-the-same-act (D7), which this extends. No ticket in the corpus covers the tester's caster skipping the check (grep of outlinecheck in red_tickets.py finds nothing).
challenge.real_collision: RULE 1: the tester may not import cairn.devices.codemother. The command 'cairn outlinecheck <ticket>' is in outline_check's declared public_interface, so the subprocess call is the published door.

answers.falsifier: A tester-cast red ticket in a scratch world passes inspector.buildme_rides_the_outline_check with the record committed. N reds make exactly N reader calls, never two at once. A failed read still lands the cast and raises a trouble naming the ticket.
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: tickets 133df5f7de08 and 8d6936a7d080 were cast by cairn/devices/tester/red_tickets.py (decisions[0].by = tester; commons commit 0c079ac4), and akienasus's land of each stopped at the BUILDME lane the_ticket_was_checked_against_the_outline (orchestrator relay 2026-11-15)
answers.how: After each cast in ticket_what_is_new, red_tickets runs codemother's published command 'cairn outlinecheck <id>' as a subprocess, pointed at the same roots through CAIRN_ARTIFACT_ROOTS. The record and any questions it opened ride the same commit. A failed check raises a tester trouble naming the ticket, and the cast still lands. A red-first proof uses a fake reader that counts its calls.
answers.traces_to: Law 4: the outline check is a rule enforced at BUILDME, and the cast door that skips it leaves every tester-cast ticket to fail there. /sorted step 5 and outline 10.3.5.1 require the check right after the cast.
answers.what: Every red ticket the tester casts carries the outline-check record that the BUILDME lane reads, written and committed in the same act as the cast.

bullets.text: The tester's red-ticket caster never ran the outline check, so every ticket it cast stalled at BUILDME (133d, 8d69).
